chunks: Al-Ṣaffār, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Wuhayb ibn Ḥafṣ, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a group who were on a journey, and ritual impurity due to janābah befell some of them, while they had no water with them except enough for the junub to perform his ghusl. Is it better that the others perform wudu, or that they give the water to the junub so that he may perform ghusl while they do not perform wudu?
So he عليه السلام said: “They should perform wudu, and the junub should perform tayammum.”

key_terms.الْجُنُبَ: the person in a state of janābah
key_terms.سَفَرٍ: travel or journey, the situation in which this ruling occurs
key_terms.لِغُسْلِهِ: for his ghusl, the full ritual bath
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum, dry ablution in place of water purification

ai.seo_question: If travelers have only enough water for one ghusl, should it be used for the junub or for the others’ wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for travelers with limited water when one person is in janābah and the rest need wudu. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rules that the available water should be used for the others’ wudu, while the junub performs tayammum, showing the practical prioritization of ritual purity rulings under scarcity.
